issues.legal_issue: A legislature cannot make prior civil court judgments ineffective merely by directing an administrator to disregard them, but may do so by changing the legal basis on which they rest.
material_facts: Civil court decrees had recognised private rights in lands and held that those lands fell outside the village common lands regulated by the principal law.
The later amendment empowered an Assistant Collector to decide claims concerning those lands notwithstanding the earlier decrees and orders.
The amendment did not alter the legal basis on which the decrees had been made or bring the lands covered by them within the regulated village common lands.
issues.conclusion: The provisions directing the Assistant Collector to disregard the earlier decrees and orders were unconstitutional; legislative action can affect such judgments only by altering, removing or neutralising their legal basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under the constitutional separation of legislative and judicial functions, a legislature may not reverse a judicial decision by a bare declaration that it is invalid or not binding. It may render a decision ineffective by fundamentally changing the law on which the decision rests, including retrospectively. The Court followed Shri Prithvi Cotton Mills Ltd. v. Broach Borough Municipality, Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Hindustan Machine Tools Ltd., Smt. Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Shri Raj Narain, and I.N. Saksena v. State of Madhya Pradesh; referred to Misrilal Jain v. State of Orissa; approved Bajinder Singh v. Assistant Collector; and distinguished Sunder Dass v. Ram Prakash.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_legislative_: A party challenged legislation that authorised an administrator to decide claims despite earlier court judgments.
predicates.prior_civil_judgment_recognises_private_: A civil court had recognised a private party's rights in property and determined that the property fell outside the regulated common lands.
predicates.legislation_directs_administrator_to_dis: The legislature empowered an administrator to decide the property claim notwithstanding the earlier judgment.
predicates.legislation_changes_legal_basis: The legislature altered the legal rule on which the earlier judgment rested.

issues.definition: When a legislative override is challenged, an administrator is not authorised to disregard a prior civil judgment recognising private rights if the legislature has not changed the legal basis of that judgment.

issues.legal_issue: A law that operates retrospectively to nullify earlier civil court adjudications is invalid to that extent, while its prospective operation may continue if it leaves those adjudications undisturbed.
material_facts: The amendment retrospectively barred civil courts from deciding specified questions about whether land was village common land or vested in a Panchayat.
It empowered revenue authorities to decide those questions, gave their decisions finality, and purported to give those powers effect from the commencement of the principal law.
The amendment was intended to allow those authorities to decide claims despite earlier civil court decrees and orders recognising private rights.
The amendment did not alter the legal basis of those earlier adjudications.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was invalid, inoperative and unconstitutional insofar as it operated retrospectively to nullify earlier civil court adjudications. It could operate prospectively in proceedings commenced after the amendment, provided it did not disturb the finality of earlier adjudications.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may legislate retrospectively within its field, but cannot use retrospective provisions merely to nullify prior judicial adjudications; it must alter, remove or neutralise the legal basis of those decisions. Prospective adjudication of later claims is permissible if it does not disturb earlier final adjudications. The Court relied on Shri Prithvi Cotton Mills Ltd. v. Broach Borough Municipality, Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Hindustan Machine Tools Ltd., Smt. Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Shri Raj Narain, and I.N. Saksena v. State of Madhya Pradesh; referred to Misrilal Jain v. State of Orissa; approved Bajinder Singh v. Assistant Collector; and distinguished Sunder Dass v. Ram Prakash.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_retroactive_claim_law and prior_civil_adjudication_exists and law_operates_retrospectively_to_nullify_adjudication and not law_changes_legal_basis

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_retroactive_: A party challenged a law that assigned property claims to an administrative decision-maker and purported to apply retrospectively.
predicates.prior_civil_adjudication_exists: A civil court had already finally adjudicated a claim concerning the property.
predicates.law_operates_retrospectively_to_nullify_: The law purports to apply to earlier periods and allows the administrative decision-maker to undo the effect of the earlier adjudication.
predicates.law_changes_legal_basis: The law changes the legal rule on which the earlier adjudication rested.

issues.definition: If a challenged law retrospectively nullifies an earlier civil adjudication without changing its legal basis, its retrospective operation is invalid, although later proceedings may be governed by the law if earlier finality remains undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: Appeals and petitions concerning provisions that have been replaced during their pendency are infructuous when the challenged provisions no longer survive for consideration.
material_facts: The pending appeals and special leave petitions challenged judgments concerning provisions introduced by an earlier amendment.
A later amendment substituted the disputed provisions while those matters were pending.
The Court found that the earlier provisions no longer survived for consideration.
issues.conclusion: The appeals and special leave petitions concerning the superseded provisions were dismissed as infructuous.
issues.legal_principle: Where legislation has been amended so that the provisions challenged in pending proceedings no longer exist in the form under review, the challenge to those provisions does not survive for consideration.

predicates.pending_appeal_or_petition_challenges_am: A party had an appeal or petition pending that challenged provisions of an earlier amendment.
predicates.later_law_replaces_challenged_provisions: A later enactment replaced the provisions challenged in the pending proceeding.

issues.definition: A pending appeal or petition challenging amended provisions is dismissed as infructuous when a later law replaces those provisions.
